quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close together while maintaining safe space?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning, entering, or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Drivers may look directly at you and still not see you. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: Usually makes no difference in handling.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can affect how the motorcycle handles.
Is good practice for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, the stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Extra weight increases the motorcycle's weight, making it need more distance to stop. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest.

questions.question: A good rain suit:

options.text: Is not needed since you shouldn't ride in rain.

questions.explanation: Good rain suits resist tearing and ballooning at high speeds.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who lack training and are unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used for quick stops.
Should only be used on slippery surfaces.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night instead of during the day, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, ride slower and stay farther away from other vehicles. Use the headlights ahead of you to see the road. Always be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Before you carry a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show other drivers their intentions. A left arm extended straight out means the rider is turning left or moving to the left lane.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least ______.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated in Kentucky. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A car may pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a parking spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars can be dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What is true about passing in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it can be done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.question: To lean your motorcycle for a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots and help you see and be seen. It should also help you avoid surface hazards, wind blasts from other vehicles, and give you an escape route if needed. Stay positioned so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze only the front brake sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Get in the habit of using both brakes every time you slow or stop. Using both brakes makes quick stops easier and safer. If you practice this habit regularly, you will be ready if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. The best footwear for riding is lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles. Athletic shoes do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials helps other drivers see you. You should wear reflective clothing at all times.

questions.question: It is recommended that a motorcyclist:

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take rest breaks every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to daytime?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
questions.explanation: Slow down before shifting into a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, use your brakes to reach a safe speed first.
